title: Pipeline Security Gates
impact: Vulnerabilities fail the build, not production
context: Security review happened late, by hand, after code was already merged and often already shipped.
threat: Issues found after release are expensive, disruptive, and land on whoever is on call, not on the author who introduced them.
action: Wired automated security checks directly into the delivery pipeline so risky changes fail early, at the point they are cheapest to fix.
tradeoff: Adds minutes to every build and demands the checks stay low-noise, or developers learn to ignore them.

title: Merge Request Guardrails
impact: Risky diffs blocked before they merge
context: Nothing systematically inspected a change for security problems between opening a request and merging it.
threat: A single unreviewed diff can introduce an exposure that reaches production quietly and lives there for months.
action: Every change is scanned as part of review; findings are summarized inline and merges are held until the risk is resolved or accepted.
tradeoff: A blocked merge is friction; the guardrail has to be accurate enough that the friction is trusted, not resented.

title: Shift-Left Enablement
context: Developers only heard about security problems in a late audit, far from the code and the context that created them.
threat: Late feedback means rework, missed deadlines, and a security team seen as a blocker rather than a partner.
action: Moved fast, actionable security feedback into the tools developers already use, so problems surface while the code is still fresh.
tradeoff: Requires investment in developer experience: bad tooling here erodes trust faster than no tooling at all.

title: Continuous Vulnerability Scanning
impact: Standing coverage instead of point-in-time checks
context: Scans ran occasionally and manually, so coverage drifted the moment the code changed.
threat: A vulnerability introduced the day after a scan could sit undetected until the next manual pass.
action: Made static and dynamic analysis a continuous, automated part of the lifecycle so coverage tracks the code as it evolves.
tradeoff: Continuous scanning generates volume; without tuning and triage it becomes noise that buries the real findings.

title: Secrets & Dependency Hygiene
impact: Leaked keys and stale packages caught at the door
context: Credentials occasionally slipped into commits, and third-party dependencies aged silently past their safe-to-use window.
threat: A single leaked key or known-vulnerable package is often all an attacker needs to get a foothold.
action: Automated detection of committed secrets and vulnerable dependencies, blocking them from entering the codebase in the first place.
tradeoff: False positives cost developer time; rotation and upgrades add maintenance the team has to actually commit to.
